title: Primitive-root charts for the finite purity coefficient sources
statement: In [def-pur-conventions], for $1\le m\le n$ use the actual quotient $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ and its derived scalar extension. Finite-Tor constructible inputs retain that property [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For every primitive $\ell^n$ root $\zeta$ in the fixed algebraically closed base, define the coefficient-root-line chart by $a\mapsto a\otimes\zeta$ on constant sections of the finite twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Use the ordered tensor and shift composites of [def-pur-finite-reduction-chart-calculus] to obtain its $d$th shifted power chart. Comparison inverse image and intrinsic realization give the chart $Lf^*K(d)[2d]\simeq(Lf^*K)[2d]$ for the exact source of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. This construction uses roots, tensor, shifts and ordinary pullback only, independently of purity or exceptional inverse image.

source.place: Operation, root-line, twist and shift comparisons; finite-reduction proof

proof.text: For finiteReduction_preserves_ctf, apply the constructibility and same-Tor-interval clause of det-sp-scalar-extension-functor to the actual quotient ring homomorphism. The two quotient rings are finite and are killed by ell^n and ell^m, respectively: diagonalExponent_annihilates gives the zero scalar, hence its action on every ring element vanishes. Unpack and repack the bounded-constructibility and finite-Tor predicates.

Construct the forward root-line map by sheafifying the linear map a ↦ a times the root section. For the inverse, compose the inverse primitive-root isomorphism with the scalar map Z/N → A and the constant-sheaf unit; the extension/restriction adjunction and sheafification give the inverse linear sheaf map. The first inverse identity is checked on constant A sections. The second is checked on pure tensors: the root sheaf map identity is checked after the primitive-root isomorphism and on constant Z/N sections, which are natural multiples of 1. Sheafification uniqueness also proves that the displayed section formula determines the isomorphism uniquely.

Compose the existing Tate reassociation, the tensor image of the root-power chart followed by the coefficient-unit chart, and the native tensor-unit shift comparison. These are the three required factors. Each normalization HEq fixes its factor, so equality of the factors gives uniqueness of their composite. Transport this chart through the existing intrinsic realization and shift comparison. Cache this ordered composite over an abstract coefficient ring. The normalization is its exact heterogeneous equality; the proved generic factor-normalization equivalence identifies this with the original existential three-factor presentation, without changing its meaning.
